findings.desc: CHK-001:edge:0 (must, type=cli): the diff-failed branch of classifyMergeLineage (packages/main/src/core/validation-lineage.ts:62-66, netDiffChangedPaths throwing after the ancestor check passes) is never actually exercised by any test. The recorded evidence (logic_test, no command) only points at smoke test 6, which exercises the SEPARATE not-ancestor catch (merge-base --is-ancestor failing on an orphan branch), not the netDiffChangedPaths catch. Grep across the repo (excluding dist) for diff-failed/lineage_diff_failed/lineage-diff-failed/netDiffChangedPaths/classifyMergeLineage shows only the 3 production files + the smoke; no test ever forces netDiffChangedPaths to throw while merge-base --is-ancestor still succeeds, so the split-catch guarantee (a diff failure surfaces a DISTINCT reason string instead of being mislabeled as not-ancestor) is unverified at runtime -- a future refactor that merges the two catch blocks or reuses the same reason string would go undetected. A reachable repro exists (e.g. delete/corrupt a tree object reachable only from one endpoint commit so merge-base --is-ancestor still succeeds via the commit-parent graph but git diff-tree fails to read the tree) but was not implemented.
findings.resolvedReason: Added injectable changedPathsFn to classifyMergeLineage + smoke test 7 that injects a throwing diff on an ancestor scenario, asserting {kind:'diff-failed'} distinct from not-ancestor. Committed 8f2eaa3208; CHK-001:edge:0 evidence updated to the runtime test.

findings.desc: validation-evidence-reuse.ts:263 and validation-evidence-admissibility.ts:48 switch over MergeLineageClassification.kind (5 variants: exact-head/trusted-descendant/untrusted/not-ancestor/diff-failed) with no default case and no exhaustiveness guard, unlike the codebase convention used for exactly this purpose elsewhere (const never: never = kind; in packages/main/src/core/usage-ledger/estimate.ts:407 and assemble.ts:115). tsconfig.json (packages/main/tsconfig.json) has strict:true but NOT noImplicitReturns, so tsc will not error if a future MergeLineageClassification variant is added in validation-lineage.ts without updating both switches -- each function would silently fall through and return undefined at runtime (typed as a non-optional lineage object), and callers (evaluateRoutineValidationReuse, evaluateValidationEvidenceAdmissibility) would throw on .lineage/.reasons access instead of getting a compile-time error. Maintainability/type-safety gap on a trust-boundary classifier shared by two callers; not exploitable today (both switches currently handle all 5 kinds correctly -- verified via clean build + all smokes passing in an isolated worktree), but it removes the compiler safety net the rest of the codebase relies on for exactly this switch-exhaustiveness pattern.
findings.resolvedReason: Added default exhaustiveness guard (const _exhaustive: never = classification) to both MergeLineageClassification.kind switches in validation-evidence-reuse.ts and validation-evidence-admissibility.ts, per the codebase convention; a future variant now fails to compile. Committed 8f2eaa3208.

findings.desc: npm run test:process-fact-contract (scripts/verify-process-fact-contract.mjs:3994-3999, invoked by red-evidence-target-binding-smoke.js step 47/53 of npm test / lattice validate) FAILS on current worktree state: 5 assertion failures — shared routine validation reuse contract missing --is-ancestor, diff-tree, isStoryMetadataPath, merge-base, rev-list. The static contract reads packages/main/src/core/validation-evidence-reuse.ts raw text and requires these literal git-command tokens to be present there; CHK-001 extracted the merge-lineage classifier (including all of merge-base/--is-ancestor/rev-list/diff-tree/isStoryMetadataPath) into the new shared module validation-lineage.ts, so validation-evidence-reuse.ts no longer contains any of these tokens (grep confirms zero matches except the untrusted-lineage-path: reasons string). Confirmed this passed at the story merge-base with main (1848e37a4c) and fails now on HEAD 9d7987d — a real regression caused by this story, not pre-existing. This directly contradicts CHK-001:adversarial:2 verificationEvidence (logic_test, no command, claims "no collateral regression" based only on a git-diff read of the other 8 reuse factors) — that evidence never ran the full test suite / this specific contract check, so the collateral regression went undetected. scripts/verify-process-fact-contract.mjs is NOT in the story scope allowedModify list, so fixing this needs either a scope amendment (add the script) or a design change that keeps the tokens discoverable (e.g. re-export/comment) so the shared-classifier extraction does not silently break this pre-existing regression gate. Blocks DONE: npm test currently fails.
findings.resolvedReason: Updated scripts/verify-process-fact-contract.mjs to verify the four merge-lineage git tokens in validation-lineage.ts (shared classifier) and dropped obsolete rev-list; scope-acknowledged. Full npm test now exits 0 (test:process-fact-contract verified). Committed 72ab8ff83f.

findings.desc: CHK-001:edge:2 / CHK-002:edge:2 (must, maxBuffer robustness): validation-reuse-merge-lineage-smoke.ts:121-135 large-diff test only produces ~118KB of diff-tree -z output (1500 paths x ~80 bytes, empirically measured via reproduction), far short of the >16MB the CHK-001 checklist context requires ("a diff producing >16MB of path output does not throw ENOBUFS") and even short of Node execFileSync default maxBuffer (1 MiB). Reproduced: the identical git diff-tree invocation succeeds with NO maxBuffer override at all (default 1 MiB buffer), so this assertion provides zero discriminating power for the GIT_LINEAGE_MAXBUFFER=1024*1024*1024 fix in validation-lineage.ts:9 -- reverting/shrinking that constant would not make this test fail. The maxBuffer robustness intent is therefore unverified at the claimed scale (padding, not a genuine adversarial/edge assertion).
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed: the large-diff block now proves discriminating power directly — asserts the raw git diff-tree call throws ENOBUFS without a maxBuffer override, then asserts classifyMergeLineage/netDiffChangedPaths succeed via GIT_LINEAGE_MAXBUFFER. Verified by temporarily reverting the constant to 1 MiB: the smoke then fails, proving the test would have caught this regression.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/tasks/validation-reuse-merge-lineage-smoke.ts:148-158 (block 5, the F-004 fix): re-running the fresh build 19x on this machine, 3 runs (~16%, clustered) crashed with an UNCAUGHT `Error: spawnSync git ENOBUFS` (errno -55, signal SIGTERM) thrown from netDiffChangedPaths at line 156 or from the classifyMergeLineage internal call at line 158 -- despite the 1GiB maxBuffer override being correctly applied (confirmed via dist inspection and 15/15 clean isolated repros of the same-size diff-tree call). Root cause appears to be transient macOS pipe/mbuf pressure from block 5 issuing 3 successive large (~1.9MB) buffered execFileSync calls back-to-back within one Node process (line 153 manual measurement call, line 156 direct netDiffChangedPaths call, line 158 internal call inside classifyMergeLineage) -- none wrapped in retry or try/catch in the TEST itself (production classifyMergeLineage does catch diff failures into a clean {kind:diff-failed} result, so this is a test-only crash risk, not a production correctness bug). Since this smoke is now wired into lattice.config.json validate.commands normal tier, this is a real source of intermittent false-negative CI/validate failures (raw uncaught exception, not a clean assertion message) unrelated to any actual regression. Recommend consolidating the 3 redundant large-diff invocations in block 5 to 1 and/or adding a short retry-on-ENOBUFS around the large git call.
